summary: One concrete legacy-timing defect remains: a new post-migration change can promote an unverified legacy current-state timestamp into a measured lower bound. Existing legacy change rows remain unverified, and the inspected readers, IPC DTO, and export share the new timing representation.

findings.claim: [P2] The first new change after migration can relabel a legacy completion timestamp as a measured occurrence lower bound. insertChangeEvent takes before.observedAt directly from legacy current_file_state, then unconditionally writes timing_version=1 and returns measured timing. Migration deliberately leaves historical file_state_observations.observed_at NULL because their sample time is unknown, but that distinction is not consulted here. A modification that occurred after the old sample but before its publication can therefore be excluded by the newly asserted lower bound. The same issue affects rename/delete comparisons and the legacy path-binding fallback.
evidence: /private/tmp/ds-ci-6quvo487/project/Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/EvidenceStore.swift:2852 — occurredStart comes from before.observedAt; lines 2858–2864 substitute path_bindings.valid_from for a noncanonical alias, also without checking sample provenance.

/private/tmp/ds-ci-6quvo487/project/Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/EvidenceStore.swift:2876 — every newly inserted change is marked timing_version=1; line 2893 propagates that lower bound into the inline measured timing.

/private/tmp/ds-ci-6quvo487/project/Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/EvidenceStore.swift:3969 — legacy sample times are deliberately left NULL, while HistoricalMigrationTests.swift:168 retains current_file_state.observed_at=1000 in the historical fixture.
findings.recommendation: Derive a non-null lower bound only from retained evidence that establishes its sample semantics, including the alias-binding case. Otherwise preserve an unknown lower bound while retaining the new measured upper and detection times. Extend a real v5/v6 migration fixture with a subsequent changed observation and verify the lower bound stays null through inline publication, reopen, readers, IPC, and decoded export; then verify a later comparison between verified new samples acquires the correct lower bound.
